A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoUn research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original unlearning experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and TinyImageNet, including baseline comparisons, sequential forgetting, and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical comparisons and reports an additional representation-distance analysis in Appendix C, Table 4.

M1.justification: Equation (2) changes the contrastive-loss prefactor from 1/(2N) to 1/N, changing its weight at fixed lambda. This corrects the written objective to match the unchanged Appendix B code, which already sums two directional means; it does not establish an implementation change. The architecture and unlearning procedure remain otherwise unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three datasets and retain random, class-wise, and sequential forgetting scenarios. The added centroid analysis uses existing CIFAR-10 coverage rather than introducing a new task or population.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark and integration comparisons retain the same methods, including BadT, SSD, SCRUB, and CU in the additional-baseline comparison. The new centroid diagnostic uses already evaluated Original, Retrain, and FT models. Boundary unlearning is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds an analysis protocol that groups forget samples by class, averages distances to retain centroids, and normalizes those distances. The projection-dimension sweep is removed. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. The new analysis has an unresolved setting discrepancy: Table 4 says class-wise forgetting, while its discussion says 10% random forgetting.

E4.justification: v3 adds a centroid-distance diagnostic and an Original-model representation visualization in Appendix C. It removes v1 Appendix F.7's projection-head dimensionality ablation. The batch-size ablation is retained and moved into Section 4.3, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging results over 10 trials and retain the same uncertainty reporting in corresponding tables. The new 'Statistical Comparisons' subsection reports descriptive distances, without adding confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All nine original tables retain their numerical entries after matching renumbered tables. New Table 4 reports average distance discrepancies from Retrain of 0.017 for CoUn and 0.033 for FT. v3 removes the projection-dimensionality results, including the slight benefit and approximately 10-TFLOP overhead reported for a 512-dimensional projection head.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the contrastive loss changes its normalization in Equation (2). Theorem 1, Lemma 1, and the lemma's proof remain unchanged, with the proof moved from Appendix E to D. Added explanations of alignment and the bound's parameters do not constitute a new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: retain-only contrastive and supervised unlearning, a semantic-similarity explanation, stronger unlearning performance, and improvements from integrating CL into baselines. The abstract's added code-access statement does not change these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Figure 4's caption newly generalizes that CL improvements increase at 50% forgetting, although its NegGrad+ results include exceptions: CIFAR-100/VGG-16 decreases from 37.2% to 33.9%. The projection-head performance/cost discussion is removed. The central mechanism explanation and Appendix H limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 identifies the OpenReview submission's supplement as the code location and documents grouping and normalization for the new centroid analysis. It removes the projection-head experiment's implementation details. The supplied PyTorch code, hardware, and retained training hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al.'s 'Boundary unlearning: Rapid forgetting of deep networks via shifting the decision boundary' to the introduction and references. The related-work taxonomy and positioning against prior contrastive unlearning remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds brief explanations in Section 3.4, edits several experimental paragraphs, swaps the proof and implementation appendices, and separates architecture details into a subsection. It also promotes the batch-size discussion into the main text. Most wording and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the centroid-distance table and Original-model plot and removes the projection-dimensionality plot. It moves v1 Table 5 to main-text Table 3 and v1 Figure 11 to main-text Figure 10, with accompanying resizing, caption edits, and reflow. The overall visual format is retained.

improvement.justification: Equation (2) now agrees with the unchanged implementation, and v3 adds quantitative representation analysis. However, that analysis inconsistently identifies its forgetting scenario, the useful projection-head ablation is removed, and Figure 4 adds a generalization with exceptions in its own results. With the principal benchmark evidence and proofs unchanged, these competing gains and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
